title: We’re testing a PvE Toggle: here’s what it means for you
body:
# We're Trialling a PvE Toggle: What It Means for You

We're happy to announce that a PvE matchmaking toggle is on its way to ARC Raiders for testing purposes.

The trial will take place between **October 13-20, 2026**, letting players pick between the standard ARC Raiders PvPvE mode and a PvE-focused mode built around cooperative play against the ARC, without other Raiders as opponents.

Before diving into what the test involves, we want to look back at how this feature came about and why we're trying it now.

## Where ARC Raiders Started

Seven years ago, when ARC Raiders was first dreamed up, it looked nothing like the game you play now.

Our early plans centered on a cooperative, raid-style PvE game built around looting. That idea ran into major obstacles, and we ultimately scrapped it in favor of the tense PvPvE extraction shooter you know today. (If you want the full backstory, check out **The Evolution of ARC Raiders EP1 - Finding ARC Raiders**.)

Once the game actually launched, though, something unexpected happened. It wasn't only fans of extraction shooters who showed up in the Rust Belt. All kinds of players found their own ways to enjoy it. People started calling ARC Raiders the "Extraction (Don't) Shooter," and it drew in a broad, varied community. That's something we're proud of at Embark Studios.

Like any live game, ARC Raiders needs to keep evolving through dialogue with its players. We want to stay faithful to the game's founding principles while also honoring the different ways people choose to play.

## What the Numbers and Feedback Tell Us

At Embark, we weigh every major decision from three angles: **what the data shows, what players are telling us, and what our instincts say.**

None of these three always wins out over the others, but we try to balance all of them together. There's no perfect formula, but as players ourselves, we aim to make the calls that serve the game and its community best.

Breaking down our player base by preferred playstyle gives us this picture:

* 37% are Friendly co-op players (a group that has steadily grown since the game launched).

* 27% are Mixed players.

* 34% are Pure PvP players (a group whose numbers have stayed steady since launch).

* More than 70% of Friendly players, and even 40% of PvP players, say they'd like fewer hostile encounters. 51% of everyone surveyed said they'd be interested in a dedicated PvE option.

* There's clear tension here: friendly players frequently try to sidestep PvP altogether, and we regularly hear complaints from various players about ratting and camping tactics.

We're watching a sizable and expanding group of Raiders come to the Rust Belt purely for co-op play and the fight against the ARC, not for confrontations with other Raiders. This group has become central to our community, and we need to figure out how to properly support them instead of forcing them to find workarounds within the existing game.

## Announcing the PvE Matchmaking Toggle Beta Test

In short, we're launching a test of a PvE matchmaking toggle. Here's how it will function:

* The test runs **October 13-20, 2026.**

* Throughout the test, players can switch between the standard ARC Raiders PvPvE mode and the new PvE mode.

* The PvE mode features **zero player-to-player damage**, with sessions **centered entirely on fighting the ARC and cooperative social play.**

* PvE sessions will combine **Solos, Duos, and Trios within the same matches.**

* We've built the system to allow **smooth transitions** between modes — play a laid-back solo PvE session, then jump into a tense PvPvE match right after.

* Certain **major conditions — Night Raids, Hidden Bunker, Locked Gate, and Frigate — will not be part of the PvE matchmaking test.** These modes are built around heightened tension and depend on the unpredictability of facing different types of players.

* Playing PvE sessions **will not impact your PvPvE matchmaking rating** in any way.

* Keep in mind that **this test is limited in scope, at least for now.** Once it wraps up, the toggle will be pulled and matchmaking will revert to its usual setup. What we learn from your feedback and the data collected will guide what happens with this feature going forward.

## What the PvE Experience Looks Like

In this test, the PvE mode lets players loot, tackle quests, and explore the world without facing threats from hostile players. **Our goal here isn't to rework PvE difficulty or experiment with new progression systems — it's simply to offer players an alternative to PvP confrontations.** That said, we'll absolutely be paying attention to your feedback after the test to figure out where this feature should go next.

A few things will be different in the PvE mode:

* Overall loot value has been reduced to balance out the added safety of avoiding PvP.

* Be cautious if you're downed by ARC forces — crawling around while downed might cause them to re-target you, even mid-movement. Staying still means they'll leave you alone. This mechanic is meant to preserve some sense of danger, since the threat of other players is removed.

## The Risks and How We're Balancing Them

We want to be upfront that this test isn't without risk. The very first, never-released version of ARC Raiders was a PvE game, and we've been cautious about revisiting that direction. Adding a PvE matchmaking toggle could dial down some of the tension the game was originally designed around. Still, we have to acknowledge that many players want to experience the game their own way, and we can't dismiss what the data is showing us.

As developers, we build a game with a vision for how it's meant to be played. But once it's out in the world, it truly becomes the players' game. That's part of what makes making games so rewarding — we create something with a clear intent, then watch as players discover their own paths through it.

This PvE Matchmaking toggle test is our way of acknowledging that players' needs don't always match what we originally set out to build.

There are a few areas we'll be watching closely:

* **Player economy:** Friendly players — and PvE sessions by extension — tend to extract more often and earn more value. To offset this during the test, PvPvE sessions will get a slight bump to their baseline loot values.

* **Matchmaking and queue times:** Players in lower-population regions or those playing during off-peak hours might experience slightly longer matchmaking times. We'll be monitoring this closely to keep session quality high for everyone. Depending on how many players opt into the PvE toggle, this could also affect the quality of PvPvE sessions, something we'll be watching and adjusting as necessary.

## What Comes Next

Once the test concludes, we'll go through all the feedback and data we've gathered to decide on our next steps. Your input will play a major role in that process.

A few things we want to be clear about going forward:

* **This test might not pan out. It doesn't guarantee a permanent PvE mode**, but it does show that we're genuinely considering the possibility.

* We don't yet have a clear picture of what a future version of this feature could look like. It's entirely possible that any eventual version will differ significantly from what's in this beta test. We think this is a feature that should keep evolving alongside player feedback over time.

We intend to keep talking openly with you all, and we'll share what we've learned and what's next sometime after the test wraps up. We hope you'll jump in and tell us what worked and what didn't with the PvE matchmaking test, along with your thoughts on everything else coming in the Frozen Trail update.

Looking forward to seeing you Topside and hearing what you think.

Best,

Aleks

Executive Producer, ARC Raiders
